description: No action has more than one PENDING approval at the same time.
why_it_exists: Each end-to-end QA rerun of a drafting action raised a fresh approval request against a newer draft, leaving the older requests PENDING alongside the current one. The result was an action with several live approvals, any of which the owner could have decided - and deciding a stale one would send an out-of-date draft. QA - Approval Supersede Audit was written to clear exactly this state on one action.

expect.why_not_void: each was a genuine approval request for the draft current at the time; VOID would assert something untrue about the original request, while SUPERSEDED records what actually happened - it was neither approved nor rejected.

assertions: Grouping Approvals rows by action_id, no group contains more than one row whose upper-cased status is PENDING.
An approval that has been overtaken by a later draft is marked SUPERSEDED with decision SUPERSEDED, not VOID, REJECTED or blank.

Superseding must be read-before-mutate: refuse if the target is absent, appears more than once, is already SUPERSEDED, is any status other than PENDING, or belongs to a different matter than the authorised one.
Superseding must be refused entirely unless the approval that is meant to survive is present exactly once and PENDING - leaving an action with no live approval is worse than leaving stale ones.
Each supersede writes exactly one audit Events row with event_id 'EVT-APPROVAL-SUPERSEDED-' + approval_id, so re-running updates that row rather than appending another.
target_unresolved_reason: kind is "invariant": not executed by harness/run.js.
